analysis:
Reviewed the head text of provider-swift/Tests/DarkbloomCLITests/SandboxSetupTests.swift (lines 1-906). The change is test-only: it adds free-space-note tests (lines 236-273) and rerun, plan-offer, unattended-apply, job-running and offline scenarios (lines ~593-817), and modifies a few expected strings. No production code is changed in these units.

The tests bear on the TB-013 / T-061 installer-download surface and the Mac-owner account (A-019). Tests assert that SandboxInstaller.scriptURL refuses non-https, userinfo, query and fragment URLs (lines 52-64). They assert that validate accepts only a 200 https response with a shell shebang, and that bodies over 1 MiB are refused (lines 66-114). They assert that the staged script is mode 0600 inside a 0700 directory (lines 133-142). They assert that setup never passes --force to the installer, so running jobs are not stopped (lines 755-757, 772). They assert that without a prompt (or with --yes) only a plan that adds slots and removes none is applied (lines 735-752). These tests reinforce existing controls rather than weaken them.

Tests use a stub (CoordinatorStub) and a fake installer inside a CLICommandSandbox, so there is no real network, credential or key handling. The fake installer script and its output are test fixtures, not shipped code. No impact on A-001 through A-018, TB-002/003/007/009/011/012, or the prefix cache (T-041).

Limits: the production SandboxInstaller, SandboxSetupFlow and SandboxSizingPlan implementations were not supplied, so whether the real code actually enforces what the tests assert is unverified. The patch excerpt was truncated. The hunk at head lines 593-817 is visible in full and shows only test code. Remaining question for integration: confirm that the production changes accompanying these tests (the free-space note and the plan-offer apply logic) keep the confirmation gate for slot-removing changes and do not execute the installer with additional privileges.
